comment: The kernel's Adreno GPU (KGSL, /dev/kgsl-3d0) and the system DMA heap (/dev/dma_heap/system), bound into the container by system/plasma.config with device rules rungic-plasma writes from their current numbers. The Linux consumers are Mesa's freedreno KGSL backend (KWin, Xwayland, Flatpak's GL extension, every GL/Vulkan program), libcamera and ksystemstats: they open /dev/kgsl-3d0 read-write and the heap read-only (the container grants it read-only; libcamera's patch dmabuf-system-heap-read-only). The provider check reads the nodes' types and permissions as the desktop user, and renders a 64x64 picture offscreen through KGSL -> GBM -> EGL -> GLES (rungic-gpu-probe: nothing is shown). On a PC this is DRM's render node. Consumer side: a gap (quality/interfaces.yaml): KGSL is Qualcomm's own kernel interface with no stand-in off the phone.
